holidays.name: National Rubber Eraser Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble pink wedge that lets us pretend our mistakes never happened. Celebrate by erasing a doodle, a typo, or a questionable life choice (pencil only).
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors the invention that made pencil mistakes fixable.
holidays.funFact: Before rubber erasers became common, people rubbed out pencil marks with wads of bread. English engineer Edward Nairne is often credited with selling the first rubber erasers in the 1770s.

holidays.name: National Take a Wild Guess Day
holidays.description: A day that rewards hunches, gut feelings and bold, unsupported answers. Guess how many jellybeans are in the jar, what's for dinner, or who's calling. Being wrong is part of the fun.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to trust their instincts and enjoy not knowing for sure.
holidays.funFact: Estimating is a real skill. In a famous 1906 observation by Francis Galton, a crowd at a county fair guessed an ox's weight, and the average of their guesses landed within about one percent of the true figure.

holidays.name: National That Sucks Day
holidays.description: A permission slip to complain about the small stuff, like stubbed toes, soggy fries and slow Wi-Fi. You acknowledge the bad thing, say "that sucks," and move on, ideally with a laugh.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It falls on April 15, which is also Tax Day in the U.S., so the timing fits.
holidays.funFact: The date lines up with Tax Day in the United States. That makes it a convenient moment for a collective groan.
